headline: 29 public server configurations checked (28 servers; GitHub with default and all toolsets), plus this repo's best and rich. 10 are portable on every client measured: Cloudflare docs, Exa, OpenAI docs, GitMCP, Astro docs, Playwright, Chrome DevTools, Kubernetes, mcp-atlassian and Sentry (hosted).

Server instructions are the most common problem: 12 of the 29 ship more than 512 characters (632–6,731). Two keep their guidance there, so claude.ai chat and ChatGPT Work get little more than tool names: DeepWiki (3,097 against 212 in all descriptions) and Terraform (4,295 against 3,497).

The worst real cases. AWS API: its two tools (call_aws, suggest_aws_commands) lose 36–38% of their descriptions on Claude Code. MongoDB: four core query tools (aggregate, create-index, explain, export, 9–12k schemas) lose all 21–31 parameter describes on Codex and ChatGPT Work.

The worst are hosted: Notion (45 tools, 242k chars of tool definitions per turn; notion-update-page 9,425-char description, 78% cut on Claude Code; notion-query-data-sources a 75,908-char input schema whose 537 describes Codex drops; 12 of 45 tools red) and Vercel (243 tools, 561k chars per turn; 15 schemas over 5,000, create_connector 54,341). Canva generate-design loses 64% of its description on Claude Code.
Tool definitions re-sent per turn: up to 257k chars (GitHub, all toolsets); 74–78k for Notion, Azure, Grafana and MongoDB.
23 remote servers needed OAuth even to list tools, so the hosted versions of Notion, Linear, Stripe, Atlassian and others are not in the sample.
caveats: Static: no tool calls, so responses are not checked.
The limits are the client versions measured on 2026-09-27.
Hugging Face was read anonymously; a signed-in account may get more tools.
